Name: Artisans Guild
Type: faction
Summary: A national guild representing skilled crafts and productive trades in West, headquartered at the House of Making in Calderan's East District.
Context: Artisans Guild, House of Making, Masterworks, craft certification, masters, workshops
The Artisans Guild encompasses many artisan professions rather than a separate major national faction for each craft; it covers far more than smiths. It may maintain local city branches with local representatives, who collectively determine or select a national representative. Selection methods remain undefined. Branches are parts of this national institution. Specialized local associations may emerge later; none are authored now. Its headquarters is the House of Making in Calderan's East District, which handles guild administration, certification, masters, workshop politics and records, and gives access to rare tools and high-value specialist workspaces, the Masterworks. It keeps a representative office near the Ducal Citadel in Center, and an Artisans Guild representative holds one of the nine seats of the Ducal Council of Calderan; the current representative is Brunna Keld. Noble houses may influence the Guild without being part of it.

Name: Beastfolk
Type: world_lore
Summary: Beastfolk are a broad umbrella of animal-associated lineages; prejudice against them is common in human-dominated West.
Possible lineages include feline, canine, vulpine, lupine, and other familiar variants; this list is non-exhaustive. Human-dominated society in West commonly treats Beastfolk as socially inferior. This is West social prejudice, not biological truth. Beastfolk there are disproportionately found among enslaved populations, agricultural labor, hard manual work, combat-related exploitation, and vulnerable social classes. Not every Beastfolk is enslaved. This social pattern is not universal across the world; Center, East, and future continents may have different relationships with Beastfolk, presently undefined.

Name: Blackwater
Aliases: The Unchained Haven
Type: location

Summary: Blackwater, The Unchained Haven, is a criminal maritime enclave on West's southwestern coast, outside effective normal direct West control.
Its dark coastal/cliff environment supports a persistent maritime criminal culture. Conventional state governance is weak or absent, but power exists in fragmented, unstable competition among smuggling interests, pirate captains, and criminal cartels. Black-market commerce includes fencing stolen goods, illegal slave traffic, transfer or sale of unregistered or stolen captives, and people kidnapped from neighboring nations. Geographic containment in West does not imply effective direct political control. Calderan dislikes and distrusts Blackwater but pragmatically tolerates some of its existence for dirty economic value, absorption of crime, indirect maritime defense/interdiction, and keeping worse external threats at distance. Tolerance is not lawful endorsement or a formal treaty. Blackwater's persistent maritime/commercial rivalry with Sandspear involves Sorrow Sea and Chained Bay routes, smuggling, piracy/corsair activity, protection rackets, captured cargo, slave traffic, and wartime spoils. Their ships sometimes fight bloody naval engagements; this is not formal West–Center naval war, and no winner is predetermined.

Feature: fragmented criminal governance. Competing smuggling interests, pirate captains, and criminal cartels exercise unstable power; no formal council is established.

Name: Calderan
Type: location
Parent: West
Summary: Calderan is the inland capital and largest city of West, the realm's political, economic and institutional center and the main campaign city, governed by the Duke of Calderan in the Sun Emperor's name.
Context: Calderan capital and main campaign city of West.
Calderan lies in the northern/central-western interior of West. The established five-district model applies here: West, East, North, South, and Center are predominant social/economic themes, not exclusive zoning. The Sun Emperor is the sovereign of West but does not reside in Calderan. Duke Uther Calderan governs the capital in his name from the Ducal Citadel, advised by the nine-seat Ducal Council of Calderan; civic arrangements also include the national guilds, the Church of the Sun Emperor, whose High Archon of the West sits in Calderan, the City Guard and the magistracy. Calderan has four cardinal main gates, the Imperial Gate in South being the largest and most tightly controlled; entry needs a writ but no general entrance tax. Calderan and Davenport together hold principal institutional/legal control over West's slave market. The full legal constitution of that monopoly remains undefined. Calderan regards Blackwater as a politically awkward necessary evil: disliked and distrusted but pragmatically tolerated for dirty economic value, absorption of crime, indirect maritime defense/interdiction, and keeping worse external threats at distance. This is not blanket lawful endorsement or an established treaty. Calderan is West's largest city, a very large, dense walled metropolis. Its five districts are broad regions, not neighborhoods. Crossing substantial parts of the city is meaningful travel. Center is enclosed by an older inner wall. Calderan has approximately 100,000 inhabitants and is the second most populous city known globally. Its roughly oval urban footprint has four outer districts surrounding Center. Crossing most of the city cardinal-to-cardinal on foot takes approximately two hours, possibly somewhat less. From Heartstone, ordinary walking takes approximately 30 minutes to Main Market Square, 40 minutes to Calderan Central District and 20 minutes to Calderan Slave Market. These are approximate scale references, not exact routes or travel connections.
Feature: capital of West. West's principal national political center.
Feature: four cardinal gates. Four main gates in the outer walls, one per cardinal direction. The southern Imperial Gate is the largest and best defended; the other three handle more local or specialized traffic under the same general entry rules.
Feature: five-district civic structure. West, East, North, South, and Center Districts retain their established non-exclusive themes and civic institutions.
Feature: legal slave-market control. Calderan and Davenport share principal institutional monopoly/control over West's legal slave market.

Name: Center District
Display name: Calderan Center District
Aliases: Calderan Center District
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: Center District is Calderan's political, administrative, noble, financial and prestige district, a roughly circular area behind its own inner wall around the Ducal Citadel, and the best-maintained part of the city.
Context: Center District of Calderan, Central District, urban district, inner wall, Ducal Citadel, Duke, nobles, banking, Gilded Row, Fountain Court, Civil Registry, Ducal Archive, High Courts.
Center is Calderan's wealthiest and politically most important district: political, administrative, noble, financial and prestige functions concentrate here. It is roughly circular and enclosed by an older inner wall, tall and well maintained though less massive than the outer city walls, used for access control and symbolic separation. It is the best-maintained district: immaculate, well-paved streets, gardens, fountains, decorative public works, oil street lighting, prestige architecture and little industrial noise. The Ducal Citadel, residence and seat of Duke Uther Calderan, is its political center, surrounded by the administrative core: the Calderan Civil Registry, the Ducal Archive, the Office of Holdings and Title and the High Courts of Calderan. The Merchants Guild, Artisans Guild, Learned Arts Guild and the Church of the Sun Emperor keep representative or liaison offices near the Citadel for political business; their headquarters are elsewhere. Center is Calderan's financial district, where formal banking houses and elite private lenders and merchant-financiers coexist; House Morvath is deeply involved in major finance. Gilded Row is the principal prestige retail street and Fountain Court a small elegant civic square. Noble households concentrate here, but Center is never exclusively noble. These are predominant tendencies, not exclusive zoning. Crossing substantial parts of a district is meaningful travel; no exact roads or navigation routes are established.
Feature: inner wall. A tall, well-maintained inner wall, less massive than the outer city walls, encloses Center for access control and symbolic separation.
Feature: four inner-wall gates. Four principal gates, broadly aligned with the major directions, pierce the inner wall; minor service access points may also exist. By day ordinary people may enter on legitimate business and guards can question or identify visitors; at night access becomes substantially more restricted. Center is not closed to commoners.
Feature: oil street lighting. Oil lamps light Center's streets, which are better paved and kept than anywhere else in Calderan.

Name: East District
Display name: Calderan East District
Aliases: Calderan East District
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: East District is Calderan's manufacturing, industrial-artisan and large-scale commercial heart, a dense low-rise district of workshops, smithies, foundries and craft halls under persistent furnace smoke, and home to The Crucible, the largest market in West.
Context: East District of Calderan, urban district, manufacturing, where goods are manufactured, workshops, foundries, smithies, clockwork, metallurgy, dwarves, The Crucible, Merchants' Mile, Smelter Pit.
East is dense, busy and relatively low-rise: broad workshops, smithies, foundries, timber yards, craft halls, textile houses, ateliers and metalworking shops, with no dominant skyline of towers. Smoke from charcoal, coal, furnaces and forges hangs over much of it, much of it rising from the lower-lying Smelter Pit. It is practical and laborious rather than elegant, and neither poor nor rich: workers, skilled laborers, artisans, shopkeepers and small proprietors form most of its people, alongside some wealthy workshop owners and prestigious manufacturers. Ordinary working and lower-middle-class houses, often near or attached to workshops, are functional rather than luxurious; there is no concentration of noble estates. East has the highest proportion of dwarves in Calderan without being a dwarven district: Common and Dwarvish signage is normal, robust stone and iron building is common, long-established workshop families practice strong craft traditions and traditional taverns serve dark beer. Humans, elves, Beastfolk and people of mixed ancestry are common too. East is famous beyond Calderan for fine clockwork and precision mechanics and for high-grade metallurgy. The Merchants' Mile feeds The Crucible; the Merchants Guild's House of Scales and the Artisans Guild's House of Making stand in East. Visible street crime is comparatively low and City Guard patrols are denser than in West; that does not make East morally clean. These are predominant tendencies, not exclusive zoning. Crossing substantial parts of a district is meaningful travel; no exact roads or navigation routes are established.
Feature: furnace smoke. Persistent smoke from charcoal, coal, furnaces and forges gives much of East a hazy, smoky atmosphere, heaviest around the Smelter Pit.
Feature: bilingual signage. Common and Dwarvish signage is normal on workshops, shops and taverns.
Feature: workshop warehouses. Workshops and shops keep their own storerooms and small warehouses. East is not Calderan's dominant bulk-warehousing district.

Owner: East District
Section: crime_and_security
Summary: East's comparatively low street crime, dense City Guard patrols and characteristic commercial crime.
Context: East District crime, guard patrols, fraud, off-book contracts, undeclared goods, illicit export, bribery, guild influence.
Visible street crime in East is comparatively low. City Guard patrols are denser than in West because East holds valuable goods, production infrastructure, guild interests and heavy commercial traffic. Mugging and gang violence are less characteristic than labor exploitation, off-book contracts, document fraud, undeclared goods, illicit export, commercial corruption, guild influence, regulatory evasion and bribery. Safer streets do not make East morally clean. No specific criminal organizations, officials or cases are established.

Owner: East District
Section: industry_and_labor
Summary: East District production chain, export specialties, storage flow and labor, including dwarven expertise and systemic Beastfolk slave labor.
Context: East production chain, clockwork, precision mechanics, metallurgy, alloys, armor materials, textiles, warehouses, Beastfolk slave labor, dwarven workshops, elven craft.
East handles the full production chain: raw materials, processing, smelting and preparation, components, workshop manufacture, finished goods, retail and export. Its two specialties famous beyond Calderan are fine clockwork and precision mechanics (spring mechanisms, fine gears, complex locks, precision and measuring instruments, small mechanical assemblies) and high-grade metallurgy (refined alloys, strong and light metalwork, high-end armor materials, precision components and specialist metal products). Dwarven expertise is strongly associated with both; elven craft knowledge contributes to some specialized alloying and fine work, and wood-working elves and other specialist artisans operate here. No magical metallurgy is established. Textile production is important, from everyday clothing to luxury cloth and fashion goods, many later sold in Center. Goods typically move from East workshops to local storage, then to West warehouses and internal distribution, and on to other districts or external trade; major bulk and river-linked warehousing remains associated with West. Beastfolk slave labor is common and visibly systemic in heavy work: hauling, foundry work, cargo handling, workshop logistics and other physically punishing industrial labor. Many such enslaved Beastfolk have few practical rights and are treated primarily as labor assets. Not every Beastfolk in East is enslaved; free Beastfolk live and work here as well.

Name: Calderan Entry Writs
Aliases: entry writ; visitor writ; merchant writ; caravan writ; sponsored guest writ
Type: concept
Summary: Entry to Calderan is controlled by writs issued by the civil and ducal administration and checked by City Guard and customs officers at the gates; there is no general entrance tax.
Context: entry writ, visitor writ, merchant writ, caravan writ, sponsored guest writ, gate papers, customs, Imperial Gate inspection
Calderan is not open-access. There is no general entrance tax, but entry is strictly controlled. Accepted broad categories are recognized or documented residents, sponsored guests, documented merchants and caravans, and visitors with an accepted purpose. Papers take the form of an entry writ, visitor writ, merchant or caravan writ, or sponsored guest writ. Writs are issued by Calderan's civil and ducal administration and checked by City Guard and customs officers at the gate. The Merchants Guild may certify commercial identity and cargo but cannot grant entry by itself. The Imperial Gate is the most formalized and tightly controlled; the other cardinal gates follow the same general framework but handle more local or specialized traffic, where corruption and smuggling are more plausible. Durations, fees for papers and penalties are not established.

Name: North District
Display name: Calderan North District
Aliases: Calderan North District
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: North District is Calderan's religious, medical, scholarly and regulated-magic district and its second-wealthiest after Center, built of pale worked stone and white granite around the Cathedral of the Bladed Sun, cloisters, gardens and major Church and Learned Arts institutions.
Context: North District of Calderan, urban district, Church of the Sun Emperor, Cathedral of the Bladed Sun, Saint Caldus House, The Collegium, Mage Registry, Spire Academy, Bastion of Vigilance, Pyres of the Fallen, physicians, apothecaries.
North concentrates religion, medicine, scholarship and regulated magic. It is Calderan's second-wealthiest district after Center, but it is not primarily a noble residential district. Pale washed stone and white granite, monumental religious architecture, cloisters, fountains, formal gardens, parks and clean public spaces set it apart; it has more green space and better maintenance than the other outer districts. The Cathedral of the Bladed Sun dominates it visually. The Church of the Sun Emperor, the City Guard and the Inquisition are all strongly present, and visible street crime is low. The atmosphere is superficially calm and orderly over underlying institutional control. Major institutions here include Saint Caldus House, the Church's main hospital; the Pyres of the Fallen, the principal cremation complex; The Collegium, headquarters of the Learned Arts Guild and home of the Mage Registry; the nearby Spire Academy; and the Bastion of Vigilance, the Inquisition's headquarters. Physicians, apothecaries, alchemists and herbalists are concentrated here under close supervision. Sincere treatment, competent practitioners, ineffective treatment, superstition and charlatans can coexist. Religion is not universally fraudulent and temple healing is not universally magical. Charity draws many poor and displaced people toward North's temples and Church kitchens. These are predominant tendencies, not exclusive zoning. Crossing substantial parts of a district is meaningful travel; no exact roads or navigation routes are established.
Feature: white granite and pale stone. Pale washed worked stone and white granite dominate North's monumental and institutional architecture.
Feature: cloisters, gardens and parks. Cloisters, fountains, formal gardens and parks give North more well-kept green and public space than the other outer districts.

Owner: North District
Section: medical_regulation
Summary: Licensing of private clinics, supervision of apothecaries and alchemists, and regulated medicinal warehousing in North District.
Context: North clinic licensing, unlicensed healer, apothecary records, alchemist supervision, controlled substances, medicinal warehouses, Church Auditors, Inquisition review.
Independent lay medicine is legal elsewhere in Calderan, but a practitioner may not simply open an unsanctioned clinic in North. Private clinics there require authorization shared between religious and inquisitorial oversight and Learned Arts Guild professional competence. An unlicensed North clinic is treated as suspicious and may be investigated, or destroyed if it is considered a center of illicit magic or heresy; not every unlicensed healer is automatically guilty. Apothecaries and alchemists operate primarily under Learned Arts professional structures and are heavily supervised in North. Their sales and controlled-substance records may be sealed, inspected and reviewed annually by Church Auditors and the Inquisition; no catalog of controlled substances is established. North's major medicinal and alchemical stores are mixed-property institutions held by guild-affiliated private interests, nobles or large commercial holders, not by the state. Medicinal and alchemical supply is nevertheless heavily regulated, taxed and watched, and is sometimes escorted or protected by Church-linked authorities.

Name: Calderan Slave Market
Aliases: West District slave pens; Calderan slave pens; The Slave Pens; Slave Pens
Type: location
Parent: West District
Summary: Calderan Slave Market, locally The Slave Pens, is West District's large public, legal commercial complex centered on a very large open square.
Context: Calderan Slave Market, Slave Pens, slave market, slave auction, public auction, licensed private sellers, holding pens and authorized sale documentation.
A public, legal slave market in Calderan's West District, publicly known, about 20 minutes' walk from Heartstone. Its very large square exceeds Main Market Square: practical packed earth, gravel and dirt, muddy in poor weather, sometimes dirtied by blood and animal/human traffic. This major economic center has heavy daytime traffic: buyers, sellers, slaves, caravans, handlers, clerks, guards, spectators and auctions. Slavery is legal and socially accepted; ordinary attendance is not clandestine. The complex operates around the clock, formal auctions primarily by day, direct purchases outside auction hours, much less activity at night. The general authorized public auction has no named operator. Low-level authorized clerks handle required ownership documentation at official auction sales; licensed private sellers handle or arrange their own authorized sale documentation. No routine health certification requirement is established; no systematic doctors or medical inspection are present. Licensed sellers behind/around the auction conduct private acquisitions: Korvin is generalist, Mistress Elara handles prestigious and socially useful captives, Bartolomhew specializes in Beastfolk and labor/workforce categories. They do not operate the public auction. The taboo Back Alleys and deeper criminal layer are distinct. No dominant origin or percentages: sources may include war prisoners, convicted criminals, hereditary slavery, debt, economic ruin, refugees, criminal trafficking, vulnerable Beastfolk, captured elves, bandit/criminal-associated captives and other legally processed or illicitly laundered captives. Not every refugee, Beastfolk or elf is enslaved.
Feature: public auction area. General authorized daytime auction mechanism; authorized clerks document ownership at the point of sale.
Feature: holding pens. Pens holding enslaved people before display and sale.
Feature: licensed private sellers. More private acquisitions behind and around the public auction; sellers handle or arrange authorized documentation.
Feature: documentation clerks. Low-level authorized clerks handle required official auction sale papers.
Feature: guard patrols. Guard patrols attend the public complex.
Feature: loading and unloading. Caravans and handlers load and unload amid market traffic.

Name: South District
Display name: Calderan South District
Aliases: Calderan South District
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: South District is Calderan's main traveler entrance and its military, security, land-transport and hospitality district, practical and sturdy, around the Imperial Gate, Stonewatch Garrison, the South Gaol, the Long Yard and many inns.
Context: South District of Calderan, urban district, Imperial Gate, Stonewatch Garrison, South Gaol, Long Yard, Wayfarer's Rest, inns, stables, caravans, couriers, mercenaries.
South is Calderan's main entrance for travelers and its military, security, land-transport and hospitality district, though not purely military. Its people include City Guard, soldiers, innkeepers, stable and transport workers, travelers, merchants in transit and ordinary residents; newcomers and transients are a high proportion. It is broadly average in wealth, neither poor nor rich. Its architecture is practical, sturdy and neutral, less distinctive than other districts. The Imperial Gate, the city's principal land entrance, opens onto the Imperial Road. Stonewatch Garrison holds barracks, training grounds, military stables and Guard facilities; City Guard and military soldiers remain distinct institutions. Calderan South Prison, the South Gaol, is the main city prison. South is transport and logistics rather than major warehousing: stable services, carriage and wagon hire, couriers, transport contractors, farriers, caravan staging and loading yards, above all the Long Yard. East supplies many of its tools and fittings. There is no major livestock market inside the walls; large animal trade stays outside. Inns, taverns and cheap to mid-range lodgings are numerous, the Wayfarer's Rest among the largest; luxury lodging belongs mainly to North and Center. Adult prostitution is technically legal in Calderan but discreet; in South heavy Guard presence limits open street solicitation, though travelers can still find adult paid companionship and some innkeepers know how to arrange it discreetly. Mercenary work is legal and independent armed workers are easy to find in South inns and taverns; important contracts inside Calderan require registration. These are predominant tendencies, not exclusive zoning. Crossing substantial parts of a district is meaningful travel; no exact roads or navigation routes are established.

West is not uniformly poor, criminal or dangerous. Heartstone lies in north-western, more peripheral West. Toward Calderan's center, streets and buildings generally improve, guard presence increases, businesses are more respectable and residents are on average more economically stable. Toward outer West, maintenance declines, poverty and crime become more visible, refugees and street children are more common, and night travel becomes more dangerous. These are informal tendencies with no hard boundaries or official nested subdistricts. Ordinary families and successful businesses exist across the district. Grey Brook cuts through a substantial part of West, with small bridges and warehouses along parts of its banks. Main Market Square anchors ordinary commerce in the more prosperous, inner-facing part; the public Calderan Slave Market is another major economic center farther through West. Heartstone Square is primarily residential. Guards are more often feared than respected: some are harsh, overly violent or accept bribes, but this is not every guard. Between the more prosperous and outer portions, children may help family businesses, sell small goods, act as news criers, carry messages or do small jobs. This is not an official middle subdistrict. In outer West, street children are more common; some form small survival groups or gangs and some steal or pick pockets. Many are not malicious and act from poverty, abandonment, family loss or avoidance of institutions. West currently contains refugees and displaced people due in part to current frontier skirmishes. Many seek charity; a larger concentration tends toward North because of temples and religious charities. Those in outer West may seek work, beg, sleep rough or become vulnerable to crime and trafficking. Exact origins and populations are unestablished; current CampaignState overrides these current-state assumptions. Adult sex work includes low-end establishments and street solicitation in outer West, where criminal involvement or coercive economic conditions may occur; more prosperous West has higher-end adult escorts and appointment-based companionship with less visible street presence. Poor people are not inherently criminal. Outer areas are more dangerous after dark. No full newspaper system, criminal code or exact crime rates are established.

The Church of the Sun Emperor teaches that the Sun Emperor is West's divine and immortal sovereign and the bearer of purifying divine Light. It is not a guild and not one of the three civic guilds (Merchants, Artisans, Learned Arts); it is a separate spiritual-political institution with comparable or greater influence. Its character is authoritarian, bureaucratic and theocratic: ritualized obedience, institutional paranoia, purification doctrine, social control, sacrifice, duty and hierarchy. There is no rival pantheon; shrines, chapels and parish temples all belong to this Church. Its official symbol is the Bladed Sun, a stylized steel sun whose rays resemble blades, associated with Light, authority, purification, war, discipline and threat. Its national hierarchy runs from the High Archon of the West through Vicars, Auditors and Zealot Priests to Flagellants. The High Archon's seat and the Church's primary headquarters are the Cathedral of the Bladed Sun in Calderan's North District; the Church also keeps a liaison office near the Ducal Citadel. The High Archon holds spiritual authority and sits on the Ducal Council but does not replace the Duke in temporal matters. The Church runs hospitals such as Saint Caldus House, the Pyres of the Fallen and charity such as the Sun Soup Kitchens. It gives theological justification to slavery. The Inquisition is an organ of the Church. Not every priest is sadistic or corrupt; individual clergy may be sincere and compassionate.

The Church of the Sun Emperor teaches that the Sun Emperor is West's divine sovereign, founder and protector, immortal, the source or bearer of purifying divine Light, and the protector of humanity and order against corruption and Shadow. Its core virtues are obedience, duty, labor, sacrifice, endurance and social order. Suffering is not worshipped for its own sake; suffering endured in service, discipline or purification may have spiritual value, while needless suffering that destroys a useful servant of the social and divine order is waste. The body is an instrument entrusted to each person by divine order, and healing restores it to work, duty, military service, family function and social role; Church medicine is framed as restoration to proper function rather than as compassion for the individual, although individual clergy may be genuinely compassionate. Duke and High Archon are not co-rulers of identical domains: the Duke holds temporal authority (civic governance, administration, taxation, law, military and city policy) and the High Archon spiritual authority (doctrine, religious law and Church institutional matters); conflicts between them are political, not resolved by a single chain of command. Its power is administrative: high-ranking bureaucrats, magistracy and civic officials, influence over registry, archive and notarial work, administrative networks and procedural expertise. Summary: The Inquisition is the powerful, feared enforcement and investigative organ of the Church of the Sun Emperor, headquartered at the Bastion of Vigilance in Calderan's North District.

The Inquisition is institutionally intimidating and has extremely broad authority within its mandate: heresy, Shadow magic, unregistered mages, exceptional or dangerous magic, Light or Shadow users, and matters of Church security. Its national head, the High Inquisitor of the West, is based in Calderan; the Inquisition is a Church institution with substantial operational autonomy, subordinate to the High Archon's broader spiritual authority. Inquisitors are senior operational agents who may lead teams of the Inquisition Militia, its armed branch for temple security, patrols, raids and enforcement. Inquisition Clerics and Archivists handle intelligence, heresy records, mage surveillance, reports, archives and investigations. Its headquarters and national administrative center is the Bastion of Vigilance in North. The City Guard must cooperate with it under prior legal and political accords; the relationship is tense. The High Inquisitor has no permanent Ducal Council seat but may be summoned for heresy, major arcane threats or Church security. Unregistered mages are arrested, referred to it, and interrogated, examined and risk-assessed. It controls Null Dust, and it is publicly said that the Inquisition can break a mage. Its secrecy, reputation and power make it feared; it is not omnipotent or unopposed, and intervention depends on circumstances rather than following automatically from every rare spell. The current High Inquisitor of the West is Helbrecht; no individual Inquisitors are named.

Arresting a noble normally requires a formal warrant bearing the seal of the High Archon, except in obvious immediate danger or an active catastrophic threat. Wealthy merchants have no formal noble immunity but strong political protection in practice. The Iron Hands were among the earliest important dwarven groups invited into Calderan during the city's early development, arriving through ducal invitation and financial and commercial incentives; neither the date nor the Duke who invited them is established. The clan operates multiple East workshops, working somewhat like a family network under one name and shared standards. It specializes in high-grade metallurgy and preserves the production method behind an important Calderan export: a metal and alloy tradition combining unusually high strength with relatively low weight, used for armor, weapons, specialist components and precision industry. Its quality comes from alloy composition, temperature, technique, sequencing and generational expertise, not from magic, and the exact process is closely guarded clan knowledge. The elder Dunrig Iron Hands oversees the network.

It is a major military filtering point with important customs and border-control functions, high political tension, and frequent contact with the consequences of skirmishes. Official enforcement and unofficial corruption coexist. Authorities may ignore, facilitate, or inadequately investigate slave caravans originating in raids and cross-border violence. Literacy does not imply membership. Magic is a branch of this Guild; there is no separate Mages Guild. Rare and powerful practicing mages often have considerable influence, but do not automatically rule the guild. Local branches may have representatives who collectively determine or select a national representative; selection methods remain undefined. It keeps a representative office near the Ducal Citadel, and a Learned Arts Guild representative holds one of the nine seats of the Ducal Council of Calderan; the current representative is Magister Odelia Crane. Name: Light and Shadow

Summary: Light and Shadow are exceptionally rare magical classifications, not moral alignments. Church doctrine treats true Light as divine and Shadow magic as absolute heresy.
Context: Light magic, Shadow magic, Light and Shadow mages
Light is not inherently good; Shadow is not inherently evil. Both are nearly legendary in ordinary experience, known more through stories, records, rumor, and rare cases than everyday observation. They may have unusual interactions or opposition with one another; no full combat matrix is established. Publicly, the Church of the Sun Emperor teaches that the Sun Emperor bears divine Light and that true Light is a miracle or divine manifestation; mortal Light magic is not accepted as a normal magical school. In learned and arcane circles only fragmented accounts of Light users exist, usually read as legend, religious metaphor or an extinct phenomenon. Shadow magic is extremely rare, absolute heresy in Church doctrine and actively hunted. Clearly identifiable public use of either may attract major attention: surprise, fear, distrust, rumor, withdrawal, institutional interest, reports to authorities, or investigation by Church/Inquisition-related actors. Responses depend on context; no spell automatically summons the Inquisition. No Light hero, Shadow villain, or required conflict is established.

Name: Mage Registration

Magic is not outlawed. Ordinary elemental magic is tolerated and regulated, though socially suspicious, and hardline Church thought treats it as a controlled spiritual hazard: a sanctioned mage can be seen as the carrier of a dangerous condition kept under control. Anyone who demonstrates genuine mana manipulation or mage ability must be registered in the Mage Registry, housed in The Collegium, headquarters of the Learned Arts Guild. Mandatory registration is part of the historical and political compromise that lets the Learned Arts Guild and the Church coexist. An unregistered mage is subject to arrest and referral to the Inquisition, and is interrogated, examined and risk-assessed; this is not a matter of a fine. Its senior day-to-day registrar is Matthias Eld. Registration procedures, records, exemptions and the Registry's staffing structure are not established.

In a very large city, practicing mages might number in the low dozens or even roughly two hands' worth; this is a rough rarity guideline, not a demographic equation. Some respect magic, some fear it, and many unfamiliar with it distrust it. Mages often gain influence, social leverage, institutional importance, or positions associated with knowledge and power. Name: Calderan City Structure

Type: world_lore
Summary: Calderan, West's largest city and political capital, has five broad urban districts: West, East, North, South, and Center.
Context: Calderan city districts, distinct from the nations West, Center, and East.
Calderan is a very large, dense walled metropolis. Its five broad urban districts are major regions, not small neighborhoods. District themes describe predominant tendencies, not exclusive zoning: labor and harder living conditions in West; manufacturing, crafts and large-scale commerce in East; religion, medicine, scholarship and regulated magic in North; security, military, transport and hospitality in South; wealth, finance and political administration in Center. Center is enclosed by an older inner wall. Shops may exist in West, taverns in Center, and temples outside North. Crossing substantial parts of a district or the city is meaningful travel. Detailed district canon belongs to the five district locations. Exact roads and navigation routes are not established. Its population is approximately 100,000: largest in West and second most populous known globally. The roughly oval walled city has four outer districts surrounding Center. Crossing most of it cardinal-to-cardinal takes approximately two hours on foot, possibly somewhat less. Ordinary walking from Heartstone takes approximately 30 minutes to Main Market Square, 40 minutes to Calderan Central District and 20 minutes to Calderan Slave Market; these estimates do not establish precise routes.

Numerous unnamed stalls and services supply most everyday needs at low to lower-middle prices and ordinary to decent quality. Rare, elite or prestigious goods generally require East, North or Center. The Daily Grind, Blackiron Repairs & Arms, Mudlark's Herbs and Livia's Needles are four important businesses on the square. Fountain of the Fallen stands at its center and is a common meeting landmark. Second Chance Pawn and West Guard Post are nearby. The walking estimate establishes no exact route.

Name: Mana

Summary: Mana underlies magical exertion; every living person possesses it, but only a small minority can consciously use it for magic.
Possessing mana does not imply magical ability. Why some people can use it remains undefined: no genetic, divine, training, bloodline, racial, or aptitude-test explanation is established. Mana can be spent and recovered; storage or manipulation through other means may be established later. Nicco's intended maximum is 100; actual current mana is engine-authoritative and stays between zero and maximum. The player establishes attempted or known abilities; no fixed spellbook is established. Approximate expenditure anchors are 5 for minor/simple non-healing magic, such as harmless sparks for amusement; 25 for superficial healing; 50 for serious or complex healing, including deeper injury or infection; and 75 for major whole-body/systemic healing involving internal and external damage. These are consistency anchors, not fixed spell prices. The narrator may propose reasonable costs; runtime validates numbers. The only currently defined universal recovery is 25 per crossed world-day boundary, capped at maximum. A day is 1440 world minutes. Sleep or rest alone grants nothing. Other recovery must arise from established gameplay through explicit validated deltas; being low on mana does not justify free restoration. No specific recovery item, ritual, place, or technique is established.

Uther Calderan is the current Duke of Calderan and the highest temporal authority in the city, governing it in the name of the Sun Emperor, to whom he is loyal. Dukes of Calderan take Calderan as their dynastic and office surname. His authority covers civic governance, administration, taxation, law and military and city policy. He does not control Church doctrine and does not replace the High Archon of the West in spiritual matters; conflicts between them are political and institutional. He holds the first of the nine seats of the Ducal Council of Calderan, and the Ducal Citadel in Center is his residence and seat. Aging and visibly tired, he is experienced, worldly and pragmatic, and highly conscious of status and image. No wife, children or other family are established.

Polite, somewhat monotonous and occasionally over-explanatory, he genuinely likes correct procedure, ordered documents and records kept where they belong. Summary: West is the western nation, broadly mild, temperate, and greener; Calderan is its capital.
Context: West nation on the known continent, distinct from Calderan's West District.
West directly borders Center but shares no direct land border with East. Climate is a broad tendency, not uniform everywhere. Its major mapped settlements are Calderan, Ironbound, Davenport, and Blackwater; they are not its only possible settlements. West's established monarchy, Dukes, local councils, national guilds, Church, and nationally legal slavery with local regulation remain in force. Frontier tension with Center involves skirmishes, raids, territorial incidents, feuds, localized clashes, and unofficial violence, not permanent formally declared total war. Blackwater is geographically within West but outside effective normal direct control. Calderan and Davenport hold the principal institutional control over West's legal slave market.

Name: West Governance
Type: world_lore
Summary: West is a realm ruled by the Sun Emperor, its divine and functionally immortal sovereign, with Dukes governing major cities and their surrounding territories in his name.
Context: Sun Emperor, sovereign of West, Crown, Dukes, ducal councils, guilds, Church
The Sun Emperor is the reigning sovereign of West and the supreme source of legitimacy. Church doctrine holds him to be a divine and immortal sovereign; he is functionally immortal. He does not reside in Calderan, and his residence is undefined. "The Crown" refers to his sovereign authority; no royal family, succession law or named heir is established. Each Duke is the primary temporal authority of a major city and its territory beneath the Sun Emperor, supported by a local council; Calderan's council has a fixed nine-seat form, while other cities' councils remain undefined. Such councils may include local nobles, representatives of the three national guilds, and ecclesiastical representation. Local nobles exist without a standardized tier taxonomy. The four major institutional power blocs are the Merchants Guild, Artisans Guild, Learned Arts Guild, and the Church of the Sun Emperor. The first three are national guilds; the Church is not a guild but has comparable or greater political weight. Temporal and spiritual authority are separate: Dukes govern civic matters, while the Church's High Archon of the West holds spiritual authority, and neither simply outranks the other. Guilds may maintain city branches and local representatives, who collectively determine or select a national representative; selection methods and terms remain undefined. For major realm-wide matters Dukes, guild national representatives and national Church representation may be summoned or consulted in the sovereign's name. No constitution is fixed.

Name: West Guard Post
Type: location
Parent: West District
Summary: The principal West District City Guard post, near Main Market Square.
Context: The principal West District City Guard post, near Main Market Square.
West guards are more often feared than respected. Some are harsh or overly violent; some accept money to ignore offenses. This is not every guard, and ordinary patrols still suppress obvious petty crime and public disorder. Captain Doran Hale commands the West District City Guard from this post, not the whole city force. No other named guards, corruption percentages or patrol schedules are established.

Name: Slavery in West
Type: world_lore
Summary: Slavery is nationally legal throughout West, with cities able to regulate its operation and administration.
National legality and local regulation are the established framework; detailed laws remain undefined. The institution is particularly relevant to West's treatment of Beastfolk, but enslaved people can have other backgrounds. Not every Beastfolk is enslaved, and not every enslaved person is a Center war captive. Calderan and Davenport hold principal institutional monopoly/control over West's legal slave market. Frontier raids and captives may feed Ironbound and/or Khar-Dune networks, pass through legal or falsified processing, reach Calderan/Davenport markets, and move toward West destinations, plantations, or colonies. This is a broad possible flow, not a universal route or a simulation graph. Ironbound combines official border enforcement with unofficial corruption; its slave traffic is not all legal. Khar-Dune intermediaries may falsify provenance. Blackwater is especially associated with illegal/unregistered trafficking, kidnapping, smuggling, and stolen captives; Sandspear may participate through corsair/criminal networks. Legal processing does not establish a lawful origin for every captive. Plantations and colonies exist within West's broader economic system, but their locations, sizes, ownership, crops, and political status remain undefined.

Name: Woodsigner
Aliases: Woodsigners; Woodsigner clan
Type: faction
Summary: The Woodsigners of Calderan are a small branch of a much larger Wood Elf clan, known for fine woodcraft and highly regarded bows.
Context: Woodsigner, Woodsigners, Wood Elf clan, elven bows, woodcraft, bowyers, Arwen Woodsigner, The Bent Bough
The Calderan Woodsigners are a small branch of a much larger Wood Elf clan whose wider history is not established. The branch came to Calderan through ducal invitation to contribute specialist woodcraft; neither the date nor the inviting Duke is established. Its members are relatively few and long-lived. Internally it is comparatively egalitarian, without a rigid clan-chief structure. Its specialties are bows, fine woodcraft, weapon stocks, precision wooden components, decorative carving and specialist wooden goods, and Woodsigner bows have an excellent reputation. Arwen Woodsigner works at The Bent Bough in East.

Summary: Restricted: a private Woodsigner cultural tradition about the origin of Beastfolk.
Context: Restricted Woodsigner clan tradition
A private cultural tradition preserved by the Woodsigners holds that Beastfolk ultimately descend from, or were transformed or mutated from, ancient Elves or Wood Elves. This is an inherited clan belief and knowledge claim, not established world truth; it is not public knowledge, and nothing in canon confirms or refutes it.

Name: Zul-Rath
Type: location
Parent: Center
Summary: Zul-Rath is Center's capital and major political center in the arid nation's northern/central interior.
Zul-Rath participates indirectly in Center's wider economic and military system. It may employ or tolerate forces such as Sandspear's corsairs when useful, including disruption of shipping and West trade without formal national war. Khar-Dune intermediaries may route captives toward labor sites, works, or pits associated with Zul-Rath or Center. Its ruler, dynasty, government system, districts, religion, exact architecture, detailed economy, and demographics remain undefined.
Feature: capital of Center. Center's major national political center.
